## TL;DR

::: {.callout-note}
## The paper
[epiaware.org/ComposableProbabilisticIDModels](https://epiaware.org/ComposableProbabilisticIDModels)
:::

- Modelling evidence for policy has to be timely, rigorous, and
  collaborative. Most of what we build manages two of the three
- **Chaining** models keeps you flexible and loses information.
  **Joint** models are rigorous and produce something nobody can take
  apart
- **Composable** parts can be both. Validate each part on its own, then
  compose them and fit everything together
- We built a proof of concept in Julia on Turing.jl and used it to
  rebuild `EpiNow2`, a package I maintain, out of parts that already
  existed
- I am now less sure the backend should be a probabilistic programming
  language at all. The last third of this talk is why
